WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
“In those days the LORD began to send against Judah Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah.” 2 Kings 15:37
With Pekah he besieged Ahaz in Jerusalem, “but could not overcome him”. 2 Kings 16:5
“Rezin king of Syria recovered Elath to Syria, and drave the Jews from Elath.” 2 Kings 16:6
Isaiah to Ahaz: “fear not … for the two tails of these smoking firebrands, for the fierce anger of Rezin with Syria, and of the son of Remaliah”. Isaiah 7:4
“For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin.” Isaiah 7:8
“The king of Assyria went up against Damascus, and took it, and carried the people of it captive to Kir, and slew Rezin.” 2 Kings 16:9
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
Chronicles: after his defeat Ahaz “sacrificed unto the gods of Damascus, which smote him”. 2 Chronicles 28:23
Alliance with Pekah of Israel against Ahaz: “Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah, have taken evil counsel against thee”. Isaiah 7:5
Their plan: a king of their own choosing in Judah, “the son of Tabeal”. Isaiah 7:6
When the alliance was reported, Ahaz's heart “was moved, and the heart of his people, as the trees of the wood are moved with the wind”. Isaiah 7:2
He drove the Jews from Elath. 2 Kings 16:6
Chronicles: the king of Syria carried “a great multitude” of Judah captive to Damascus. 2 Chronicles 28:5

FROM THE ASSYRIAN RECORDS: KING BY ABOUT 738 BC

His accession is not dated. He is named in Tiglath-pileser III's tribute list beside Menahem of Samaria, whose tribute Mack (1915) dates to 738 BC; the Assyrian eponym list sends the army “against Damascus” in 733 and 732 BC, and Kings says the king of Assyria took Damascus and slew Rezin.
To Edom
T. Nicol, ISBE (1915); Ellicott's Commentary

“Syria” and “Edom” look alike in Hebrew writing. Ellicott notes that the Hebrew margin, many manuscripts, the Greek and the Latin read “Edomites”; Nicol writes that “it is agreed” to read Edom. 2 Kings 16:6 [17][30]
Both: Syria took it, Edom returned
David Kimchi, as reported by John Gill (1748–1763)
Kimchi explains that the word is written “Syrians” because the king of Syria took the city, and read “Edomites” because by his means the Edomites returned to it. 2 Kings 16:6 [31]

Every passage

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not name Rezin's father or say how he came to the throne.
Scripture gives no length of reign; it says only that the king of Assyria “slew Rezin” (2 Kings 16:9), not how.
Isaiah's “burden of Damascus” (Isaiah 17:1–3) does not name him.
No Assyrian text used here describes his death; the tablet said to record it is lost.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON
From the textRezin king of Syria in the days of Ahaz; not the Rezin whose “children” were among the Nethinim who returned from exile (Ezra 2:48; Nehemiah 7:50). 2 Kings 16:5 Ezra 2:48
